title: Import preview
summary: Turn an untrusted project file into a useful preview and an all-or-nothing import.
outcome: A validated import flow with row errors, an explicit merge policy, and no partial writes.
prerequisites: Finish the first two projects. Inspect src/db/repos/dataRepo.ts and existing backup validation before changing formats.
model: Preview: normalized records, row errors, and create/update/skip counts.
Choose one duplicate policy for IDs within a file and a separate policy for IDs already stored locally.
boundaries: File reader → parse JSON → Schema decode → relationship checks → preview → transactional import. Preview performs no writes.

milestones.title: Decode files and explain row errors
milestones.brief: Validate an entire project file before giving the user an import button.
milestones.explanation: JSON.parse only checks JSON syntax. A TypeScript cast does not validate runtime data. Decode the envelope, version, and each record, then check relationships and duplicates. Bound input size and row counts so validation itself cannot freeze the interface.
steps: Create fixtures for a valid file, broken JSON, unsupported version, duplicate ID, invalid name, and orphan milestone.
Read unknown input, decode it, and display errors with record number and field. Use a file-size limit and a documented maximum record count.
Show create/update/skip totals for valid input. Keep the confirm action unavailable when validation fails.

checks.label: Every malformed fixture produces an actionable error without a write.
A valid file produces accurate preview counts.
Oversized input is rejected before expensive processing.

milestones.experiment: Put a malformed record at the end of an otherwise valid file. Verify the earlier rows have not been imported.
milestones.review: Keep syntax, schema, and relationship failures distinguishable. Do not include raw sensitive record contents in logs.
milestones.stretch: Offer a downloadable validation report with row numbers and messages.

milestones.title: Confirm an atomic merge
milestones.brief: Import the preview with an explicit duplicate policy and no partial merge.
milestones.explanation: A preview can go stale while the user reads it. Recheck the relevant data inside the import transaction, or reject and regenerate the preview if the baseline changed. Repeating the same import should have a defined result instead of silently duplicating records.
steps: Specify how existing IDs are treated: skip, reject, or update only when a version rule permits it. Show that policy in the confirmation UI.
Validate the final merge and write projects and milestones in one transaction. Prevent double submission and report committed counts.
Fail a write in the middle, retry, then import the same file again. Compare stored identities and relationships after each attempt.

checks.label: A mid-import failure rolls back all imported rows.
Repeated import follows the displayed duplicate policy.
Changes made after preview trigger revalidation or a refreshed preview.

milestones.experiment: Preview an update, edit the same project in another tab, then confirm. Verify the newer edit is not silently overwritten.
milestones.review: Identify the point where the operation becomes durable. An optimistic success toast before commit is misleading.
milestones.stretch: Add an import receipt containing the file digest, policy, counts, and completion time.

milestones.title: Prove export and restore
milestones.brief: Restore exported project data into an empty store and verify it through the actual interface.
milestones.explanation: An export that downloads successfully may still omit relationships or progress. Restoration is the real test. Compare stable business fields and a complete user journey; timestamps that intentionally change during import need an explicit comparison policy.
steps: Create a fixture with active and archived projects, ordered milestones, and linked evidence. Export it through the normal UI.
Restore into an independent empty browser store, then search, open, edit, and reopen the imported work.
Document the format version, included data, and handling of a newer unsupported file. Keep existing Recall backup compatibility intact.

checks.label: Identity, relationships, ordering, and completion survive a round trip.
Restored records remain editable and exportable.
An unsupported future version fails without changing the target store.

milestones.experiment: Remove one field from the export serializer and confirm that the round-trip test detects the lost information.
milestones.review: Verify the restored data, not just a success message. Include migration behavior for old backups when extending the real Recall format.
milestones.stretch: Add a fixture for the previous format and prove an explicit migration preserves its meaning.

milestones.title: Handle real CSV input
milestones.brief: Add a CSV import path that handles quoting, multiline fields, empty cells, and explicit column mapping without silently losing information.
milestones.explanation: CSV is not reliably parsed by splitting lines and commas. Quoted fields may contain both. Parsing yields strings; decoding supplies domain meaning. An empty cell, missing column, and the literal text null are different inputs unless your contract deliberately normalizes them. Preview that normalization before a write.
steps: Create fixtures containing commas inside names, quotes, multiline goals, blank rows, a byte-order mark, and missing headers. Declare the supported delimiter and encoding.
Use a parser with a documented dialect, map columns explicitly, then reuse the project validation boundary. Report physical or logical row numbers consistently.
Preview normalized values and confirm the transaction only after all required mappings are present. Round-trip a multiline field and compare its exact text.

checks.label: Quoted commas and multiline values survive parsing.
Missing required columns block import with actionable diagnostics.
CSV and JSON imports enforce the same domain validation.

milestones.experiment: Put a line break inside a quoted goal and an invalid record after it. Verify the diagnostic identifies the intended record without shifting later values into wrong columns.
milestones.review: Review parsing, normalization, and validation as separate stages. Document spreadsheet formula interpretation if you also export user text to CSV.
milestones.stretch: Support a mapping preview for files whose column names differ from your application's field names.

milestones.title: Keep large imports responsive
milestones.brief: Process a large file with bounded memory and progress while preserving the promised import transaction semantics.
milestones.explanation: A stream can reduce memory use only if later stages do not collect everything again. Decide whether preview stores normalized rows in temporary storage, scans twice, or limits file size. Cancellation before commit and cancellation after commit have different consequences. Explain those boundaries instead of implying that every operation can be undone.
steps: Set row, byte, and field-size limits using representative fixtures. Measure baseline memory and the longest interval during which the interface cannot respond.
Process bounded chunks with progress reporting and cancellation. Keep temporary staging separate from visible project data until confirmation.
Cancel during parsing, validation, and immediately before commit. Clean up abandoned staging data after restart and verify no phantom projects appear.

checks.label: Large supported files stay within the recorded memory budget.
Cancellation before commit creates no visible imported projects.
Temporary data is removed after failure and restart.

milestones.experiment: Use a file with one enormous field rather than many small rows. Verify that a row-count limit alone does not accidentally permit unbounded memory use.
milestones.review: Show actual measurements and the commit boundary. A progress bar animated by a timer is not evidence that the main thread remains responsive.
milestones.stretch: Move parsing to a worker and compare interaction latency before and after, including the cost of transferring messages.

milestones.title: Maintain a versioned data contract
milestones.brief: Support older project files through explicit migrations while rejecting unsupported future formats without any writes.
milestones.explanation: Versioning is a promise about meaning, not just a number in JSON. Migrations should be deterministic transformations of data, followed by current validation. Keep examples of every supported format in source control and distinguish omitted optional values from required values that did not exist in an older version.
steps: Define version 1 and version 2 fixtures with a renamed field and one new required field. Document defaulting and information-loss decisions.
Dispatch by formatVersion, migrate supported old data, and decode the final shape. Reject unknown versions before merging anything into storage.
Run old-to-new import, new export, and fresh-store restore. Compare semantic fields and preserve project/milestone identities across all transformations.

checks.label: Every supported historical fixture imports with the documented meaning.
Unknown future versions leave the store untouched.
Migration and export preserve stable identities and relationships.

milestones.experiment: Send a file labeled version 1 but containing a conflicting mixture of old and new fields. Decide whether it is rejected or normalized and test that exact rule.
milestones.review: Avoid guessing a version from whichever properties happen to be present. Record the support window and how users obtain a compatible export.
milestones.stretch: Add golden fixtures to CI and make a deliberate breaking serializer change to prove the contract test detects it.

milestones.title: Separate syntax from row errors
milestones.brief: Import malformed JSON followed by valid JSON containing one invalid project row.
milestones.explanation: A parser failure and a domain validation failure require different locations and recovery advice.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import malformed JSON followed by valid JSON containing one invalid project row. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Create distinct typed results for file parsing and row decoding.
Feed both fixtures through the same upload operation. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The malformed file reports syntax context without attempting row writes.
The valid file identifies the invalid row and field precisely.
Recovery evidence: Truncate a file halfway through its final object. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Truncate a file halfway through its final object.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the UI avoid inventing row numbers when parsing never succeeded?
milestones.stretch: Add an editor link to the exact byte or line location when available.

milestones.title: Treat decoded input as unknown
milestones.brief: Import an object whose projects property is a string instead of an array.
milestones.explanation: Static TypeScript assertions cannot establish the shape of external bytes.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import an object whose projects property is a string instead of an array. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Decode the top-level envelope before iterating project records.
Try null, arrays, strings, and missing projects properties. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Each invalid envelope produces a controlled structural error.
No uncaught map-is-not-a-function exception reaches the screen.
Recovery evidence: Provide a nested object with unexpected prototype-related keys. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Provide a nested object with unexpected prototype-related keys.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Did the agent replace validation with a type cast?
milestones.stretch: Add safe unknown-key handling and document strip-versus-reject behavior.

milestones.title: Report multiple row problems
milestones.brief: Import five rows containing two empty names, one bad timestamp, and two valid projects.
milestones.explanation: Preview should explain all independently detectable problems without changing data.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import five rows containing two empty names, one bad timestamp, and two valid projects. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Collect row-specific issues while preserving original input positions.
Compare the reported issue list with a hand-written expected list. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: All three invalid rows appear with useful field messages.
Valid rows are not mislabeled because earlier rows failed.
Recovery evidence: Correct only one row and rerun preview. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Correct only one row and rerun preview.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are issue identities stable enough to preserve focus after correction?
milestones.stretch: Add grouped issue summaries that still link to individual affected rows.

milestones.title: Normalize identity consistently
milestones.brief: Import IDs p-1, space-p-1-space, and a numeric ID in one file.
milestones.explanation: Identifier normalization must not accidentally merge distinct entities or admit invalid types.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import IDs p-1, space-p-1-space, and a numeric ID in one file. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Specify whether surrounding spaces are rejected or normalized before collision checks.
Preview the three records and inspect their interpreted identities. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Every accepted identity follows the documented string rule.
Numeric coercion never silently invents a valid project ID.
Recovery evidence: Add a second normalized duplicate later in the file. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Add a second normalized duplicate later in the file.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does duplicate detection run after the chosen normalization step?
milestones.stretch: Add a diagnostic showing raw versus interpreted identifiers for ambiguous files.

milestones.title: Bound diagnostic size
milestones.brief: Import ten thousand invalid rows each containing a megabyte-long description.
milestones.explanation: Error reporting must not duplicate the entire invalid payload into memory or the DOM.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import ten thousand invalid rows each containing a megabyte-long description. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Store concise issue codes and bounded excerpts with total counts.
Measure displayed issue count and retained diagnostic bytes. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The preview remains usable and reports the full issue total.
Raw oversized fields never appear repeatedly in error messages.
Recovery evidence: Expand the final error page and inspect its memory behavior. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Expand the final error page and inspect its memory behavior.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are diagnostics proportional to issue count rather than input-field size?
milestones.stretch: Support streaming a compact error report to a downloadable file.

milestones.title: Handle empty input deliberately
milestones.brief: Upload a zero-byte file, an empty object, and a valid backup with no projects.
milestones.explanation: Empty bytes and an intentionally empty dataset are different states.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Upload a zero-byte file, an empty object, and a valid backup with no projects. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define distinct messages and require explicit confirmation for an empty valid import.
Preview all three fixtures without touching storage. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The valid empty dataset is recognized as a valid no-op or declared replacement.
Empty bytes never become an implicit request to erase data.
Recovery evidence: Upload whitespace-only bytes after a successful preview. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Upload whitespace-only bytes after a successful preview.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the previous valid preview remain accidentally actionable?
milestones.stretch: Reset preview identity whenever a new file selection begins.

milestones.title: Preserve original row references
milestones.brief: Sort valid preview rows by name while invalid rows retain original file positions.
milestones.explanation: An error reference should continue pointing to the source record after presentation sorting.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Sort valid preview rows by name while invalid rows retain original file positions. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Keep source index separate from display index and entity identity.
Sort, filter, and expand an error for source row seventeen. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The message still identifies row seventeen in the uploaded file.
Display positions are never mistaken for source positions.
Recovery evidence: Insert a correction row before the invalid source row and reparse. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Insert a correction row before the invalid source row and reparse.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does every diagnostic belong to one immutable parse snapshot?
milestones.stretch: Show a short source excerpt beside the row reference.

milestones.title: Validate finite numbers
milestones.brief: Import revisions NaN-like text, 1e999, negative numbers, and a valid integer.
milestones.explanation: Numeric fields need finite range and integer checks beyond JavaScript number type.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import revisions NaN-like text, 1e999, negative numbers, and a valid integer. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Decode revisions through a bounded integer rule.
Preview numeric edge cases using JSON-valid exponential values. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Only values in the documented revision range are accepted.
Infinity from oversized exponents never enters storage.
Recovery evidence: Use a fractional value that looks whole after display formatting. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Use a fractional value that looks whole after display formatting.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the preview display enough precision to explain the rejection?
milestones.stretch: Add maximum safe-integer checks for counters exported by other systems.

milestones.title: Keep previews free of side effects
milestones.brief: Select a valid backup and navigate away without pressing Commit.
milestones.explanation: Decoding and previewing describe proposed changes but must not perform durable writes.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Select a valid backup and navigate away without pressing Commit. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Separate parse, plan, and commit operations with distinct service dependencies.
Instrument repository writes during file selection and preview rendering. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The preview performs zero durable mutations.
Constructing or rerendering the preview Effect never starts a commit.
Recovery evidence: Render the preview twice under development strict rendering. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Render the preview twice under development strict rendering.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does dependency construction accidentally execute insertion promises?
milestones.stretch: Use a read-only planning service type that cannot access mutation methods.

milestones.title: Bind confirmation to one plan
milestones.brief: Preview file A, then choose file B before the old confirmation button is pressed.
milestones.explanation: A commit must reference the exact file and plan the user reviewed.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Preview file A, then choose file B before the old confirmation button is pressed. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Assign a plan identity and invalidate confirmation when input changes.
Delay file B parsing and attempt to confirm the old plan. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Only the currently reviewed plan can commit.
File A's stale button cannot commit file B or vice versa.
Recovery evidence: Resolve parsing promises in reverse selection order. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Resolve parsing promises in reverse selection order.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does request identity prevent obsolete previews from replacing current state?
milestones.stretch: Include a digest and visible filename in the confirmation receipt.

milestones.title: Detect changes since preview
milestones.brief: Preview an update to project P-2 at revision four, then edit it locally.
milestones.explanation: A merge preview is stale when its assumed destination state changes.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Preview an update to project P-2 at revision four, then edit it locally. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Capture expected revisions in the plan and revalidate before mutation.
Commit after changing the destination to revision five. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The conflict is explained before overwriting local changes.
The old preview never silently wins over the newer edit.
Recovery evidence: Rebuild the preview and compare the revised conflict choice. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Rebuild the preview and compare the revised conflict choice.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the plan record assumptions rather than only final row values?
milestones.stretch: Add a three-way comparison using imported, current, and preview-base values.

milestones.title: Make duplicate IDs explicit
milestones.brief: Import two rows with ID p-8 but different names and goals.
milestones.explanation: A merge cannot choose an arbitrary winner among contradictory source identities.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import two rows with ID p-8 but different names and goals. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Reject duplicates or expose a deterministic documented resolution policy.
Reverse the duplicate rows and compare the preview. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The outcome follows the written rule independently of incidental iteration.
No hidden last-write-wins behavior decides the user's data.
Recovery evidence: Add an identical duplicate beside the conflicting duplicate. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Add an identical duplicate beside the conflicting duplicate.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the policy distinguish harmless repetition from conflicting content?
milestones.stretch: Offer a source-row comparison before resolving duplicate identities.

milestones.title: Prove all-or-nothing import
milestones.brief: Commit twenty planned changes and fail mutation nineteen.
milestones.explanation: An atomic import either applies the reviewed plan completely or retains prior state.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Commit twenty planned changes and fail mutation nineteen. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use one storage transaction for the chosen atomic policy.
Compare every affected table before and after the injected failure. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: All original rows and relationships remain unchanged.
The result never claims eighteen durable successes after rollback.
Recovery evidence: Retry the exact plan after clearing the fault. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Retry the exact plan after clearing the fault.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are relationship writes included in the same transaction as projects?
milestones.stretch: Record a committed plan receipt for later reconciliation.

milestones.title: Explain merge versus replace
milestones.brief: Import three projects into a database containing five unrelated projects.
milestones.explanation: Merge and replacement have different effects that must be explicit before confirmation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import three projects into a database containing five unrelated projects. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Show creates, updates, unchanged rows, and removals separately.
Preview both modes using the same source and destination fixtures. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The confirmation accurately predicts every affected ID.
Replacement cannot be selected implicitly by an empty or missing field.
Recovery evidence: Switch modes after inspecting a preview and attempt immediate commit. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Switch modes after inspecting a preview and attempt immediate commit.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does a mode change invalidate the prior confirmation plan?
milestones.stretch: Require a recoverable backup artifact before an explicitly chosen replacement flow.

milestones.title: Make repeated commit safe
milestones.brief: Commit a plan successfully, lose the response, and press Commit again.
milestones.explanation: Repeated delivery of one confirmed plan must not duplicate rows or increment revisions twice.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Commit a plan successfully, lose the response, and press Commit again. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Persist a plan receipt or stable command identity with the transaction.
Replay the same plan after an ambiguous response. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The second delivery reports the existing committed result.
Counters and audit events are not duplicated.
Recovery evidence: Reload between the first commit and replay. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Reload between the first commit and replay.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does command identity survive component recreation and browser restart?
milestones.stretch: Expose recent import receipts with file digest and affected-row totals.

milestones.title: Validate selected-row imports
milestones.brief: Select three valid rows from a preview where one references an unselected parent.
milestones.explanation: A selected subset must still satisfy relationship closure and domain constraints.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Select three valid rows from a preview where one references an unselected parent. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Recompute the plan for selected IDs and display required related records.
Attempt commit with the parent excluded. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The UI identifies the missing relationship before persistence.
Selecting rows never bypasses whole-file validation assumptions.
Recovery evidence: Select the parent, then deselect it while confirmation is open. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Select the parent, then deselect it while confirmation is open.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Is selection captured in the immutable confirmed plan?
milestones.stretch: Offer automatic dependency inclusion with a visible explanation of added rows.

milestones.title: Keep secrets out of merge logs
milestones.brief: Import a backup whose notes contain private tokens and customer details.
milestones.explanation: Operational logs should describe merge decisions without copying sensitive record bodies.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import a backup whose notes contain private tokens and customer details. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Log plan IDs, counts, safe error categories, and redacted identifiers.
Inspect logs from success, conflict, and rollback paths. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Logs provide enough correlation to diagnose the failed operation.
Private note content never appears in exceptions or telemetry payloads.
Recovery evidence: Force schema failure inside a field containing a token. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Force schema failure inside a field containing a token.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does generic error serialization include the rejected value by default?
milestones.stretch: Add a test that scans captured diagnostics for fixture secrets.

milestones.title: Review generated merge code
milestones.brief: An agent proposes using object spread to overwrite each destination record with imported data.
milestones.explanation: A safe merge needs an explicit ownership policy for immutable and local-only fields.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An agent proposes using object spread to overwrite each destination record with imported data. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
List allowed imported fields and preserve protected local metadata.
Import an older row lacking newly added local fields. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Protected metadata and creation identity remain intact.
Unknown source properties do not gain write authority.
Recovery evidence: Include id, revision, and sync receipt fields in the hostile fixture. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Include id, revision, and sync receipt fields in the hostile fixture.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can every assigned field be justified by the documented merge contract?
milestones.stretch: Generate a field-level plan explanation before committing the reviewed patch.

milestones.title: Round-trip relationships
milestones.brief: Export a project with tasks, evidence links, and prerequisite edges into an empty database.
milestones.explanation: A backup must preserve relationship identity as well as top-level row counts.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Export a project with tasks, evidence links, and prerequisite edges into an empty database. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define canonical export ordering and compare the restored graph.
Export, clear only the isolated fixture database, restore, and inspect links. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Every restored edge points to the intended restored entity.
Equal row counts cannot hide missing or misdirected relationships.
Recovery evidence: Shuffle serialized collection order before restore. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Shuffle serialized collection order before restore.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does restore depend on source order instead of an explicit dependency plan?
milestones.stretch: Compute a canonical graph digest for round-trip comparisons.

milestones.title: Preserve Unicode text
milestones.brief: Export names containing emoji, combining accents, and right-to-left text.
milestones.explanation: Text fidelity includes code points and ordering, not merely visually similar output.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Export names containing emoji, combining accents, and right-to-left text. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use explicit UTF-8 encoding and avoid unintended normalization during export.
Compare stored strings before and after restore by code point. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: All authored text survives byte-safe serialization and decoding.
No replacement characters or lost combining marks appear.
Recovery evidence: Open the export in a tool that adds a byte-order mark. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Open the export in a tool that adds a byte-order mark.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the decoder handle its documented encoding variants deliberately?
milestones.stretch: Add fixtures for newline styles and supplementary-plane characters.

milestones.title: Keep timestamps unambiguous
milestones.brief: Export creation and completion timestamps around a daylight-saving transition.
milestones.explanation: Portable instants need an explicit representation independent of the importing machine's locale.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Export creation and completion timestamps around a daylight-saving transition. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Serialize timestamps in a documented canonical form and validate on restore.
Restore under two different timezone settings. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Both installations recover the same instants.
Locale-formatted dates are rejected rather than guessed.
Recovery evidence: Import a timestamp without a zone offset. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Import a timestamp without a zone offset.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the contract distinguish instants from date-only deadlines?
milestones.stretch: Add round-trip tests for both field categories in one backup.

milestones.title: Exclude transient UI state
milestones.brief: Export while a modal is open, a save is pending, and a search query contains private text.
milestones.explanation: A durable backup should include intentional user data and documented progress, not arbitrary runtime state.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Export while a modal is open, a save is pending, and a search query contains private text. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Define exportable fields separately from component and request state.
Inspect the archive's manifest and records during a pending operation. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: Only committed domain data enters the durable snapshot.
Promises, error stacks, and transient search text are absent.
Recovery evidence: Complete the pending save immediately after snapshot creation. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Complete the pending save immediately after snapshot creation.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the export declare the snapshot time and inclusion boundary?
milestones.stretch: Offer a separate explicit draft export without mixing it into canonical backups.

milestones.title: Verify a consistent snapshot
milestones.brief: Export projects while a transaction moves a task between two projects.
milestones.explanation: A backup must represent one consistent state rather than a mixture of before and after.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Export projects while a transaction moves a task between two projects. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Read related tables under a supported snapshot or revision-consistency strategy.
Pause export between tables and execute the move. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: The exported graph corresponds to one valid state.
A task is never missing or linked to two contradictory parents.
Recovery evidence: Repeat with a deletion and its relationship cleanup. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.

milestones.experiment: Repeat with a deletion and its relationship cleanup.
milestones.review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can the chosen storage API actually guarantee the claimed snapshot?
milestones.stretch: Retry export when observed revisions show that a stable snapshot was unavailable.

milestones.title: Test malformed restore recovery
milestones.brief: Restore a backup with a valid envelope but an invalid relationship near the end.
milestones.explanation: A failed restore must preserve the current database under the advertised atomic policy.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Restore a backup with a valid envelope but an invalid relationship near the end. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Validate referential integrity before mutation and retain transaction safeguards.
Compare the destination snapshot before and after rejection. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.

checks.label: All preexisting destination data remains intact.
